title: Biases in LLM-Generated Musical Taste Profiles for Recommendation

bias_targets.methodology: Calculating the difference in self-recognition ratings of LLM-generated musical taste profiles between male and female users using Cohen's d to measure effect size.
Performing bootstrap simulations with linear regression models to predict user ratings of LLM-generated profiles based on the user's age as well as the mean age of their consumed songs.

Applying a Doubly Robust (DR) estimation of the Average Treatment Effect (ATE) to quantify how the presence and proportion of specific music genres (e.g., rap, metal) and track countries of origin impact user ratings of their generated profiles, controlling for confounders like prior user taste alignment.

Using linear regression to measure the association between user evaluation scores and their listening characteristics, specifically their Generalist-Specialist Score (taste diversity) and the median popularity rank of their tracked songs (mainstreamness).
